faq.a: A fault is a crack in the Earth's crust where blocks of rock move past each other. Big faults, like the San Andreas Fault in California, mark the edges of plates.

faq.q: What is the focus of an earthquake?
faq.a: The focus is the place underground where the rock first slips. The epicentre is the point on the surface directly above the focus.
asks: Where exactly does an earthquake begin?

faq.a: The rock along a fault is rough and pressed together hard, so friction holds it. The plates keep moving, so energy builds up until the friction gives way.
Aftershocks are smaller earthquakes after a big one, as the rock around the fault settles into its new position. They can go on for weeks or months.
asks: Why are there more quakes after a big one?

faq.a: Most happen along plate boundaries. About 80 percent of the biggest ones happen around the Pacific Ocean, in a belt called the Ring of Fire.
asks: Which places get the most earthquakes?

facts: The epicentre is the point on the Earth's surface directly above an earthquake's focus.
About 80 percent of the world's largest earthquakes happen around the Pacific Ring of Fire.
The San Andreas Fault marks where the Pacific and North American plates slide past each other.

quiz.say: What is the epicentre of an earthquake?

options.show: The point on the surface above where the rock slipped
options.say: The point on the surface above where the rock slipped

options.show: The deepest point of the fault
options.say: The deepest point of the fault

quiz.why: The rock slips at the focus underground; the epicentre is the surface point right above it.

wrong.1: The point underground where the rock slips is the focus, not the epicentre.
wrong.2: Waves spread out from the focus in all directions and fade with distance.

quiz.say: Why can a fault go years without an earthquake, then have a big one?

options.show: The fault is stuck while strain builds up
options.say: The fault is stuck while strain builds up

options.show: The plates stop moving for years
options.say: The plates stop moving for years

quiz.why: Friction locks the fault while the plates keep moving, so energy builds until the rock suddenly slips.

wrong.1: Plates keep moving all the time; it is the fault that is stuck.
wrong.2: Cooling has nothing to do with the timing of earthquakes.
